about: Client and server, one per navcloud region entity being streamed in (12/48 holders). Written by navcloud::RegionSystem (Update / ProcessAgents / ProcessMemoryData / MetaDataRemoval), read by navcloud::generate::GenerationSystem. Holds the region coordinates, the worker job that processes the loaded data, the asynchronous file read (navcloud.data) and a flag.

evidence.says: creator bg3.exe+0x392B120 (alloc 0x28) zeroes *(uint64*)+0 and *(uint32*)+8 (a 12-byte Vector3i); macOS RegionSystem::Update copies *(uint64*)comp and *(uint32*)(comp+8) into the processing WorkerThreadJob as the region key. Live: small ints 0..0xD (same as RegionLoadedOneFrame)
second int of the Vector3i region key
third int of the Vector3i region key; live negative values (-0x40 .. -0x4C)
not written by the creator; live garbage

macOS RegionSystem::Update: *(WorkerThreadJob**)(comp+0x10) = new job (0x70 bytes, vtable OnWTCompletion) built from the region key and the read buffer; on removal the job is waited for and freed. Windows creator zeroes +0x10. Live mostly 0 (heap in 4 samples) [offset from macOS, size/zeroing confirmed on Windows]

macOS RegionSystem::Update reads a state at *(*(comp+0x18)+0x40) (0..7, atomically set to 7 = cancelled, spins while 5) and a buffer at +0x1C0 of the same object: an asynchronous IO request for navcloud.data. Windows creator zeroes +0x18. Live always a heap pointer
Windows creator bg3.exe+0x392B120 and macOS writer both set byte +0x20 = 0; live byte 0 always 00

open_questions: meanings of +0x10/+0x18 rest on macOS pseudo-code (Windows creator only confirms two zeroed pointers there)
